assays.assay_description: Juvenile Fmr1 KO mice (P23-25) pretreated i.p. with vehicle or DPT (3, 5.6, 10 mg/kg), with or without antagonist pretreatment (pimavanserin, WAY-100635, SB-224289, methiothepin, NE-100), were placed (2 per box) in a clear polycarbonate box (46x20x20 cm) and exposed to a ~105 dB alarm for 5 min. Video-recorded; WRJ, TCS, death, latency, duration and prevalence scored visually.

application_type.evidence: Vehicle and all compounds for in vivo studies were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.) to Fmr1 KO and WT mice

setup_habituation.evidence: Juvenile mice were acclimated to the test room for 30-60 min in their home cages... placed in a clear, polycarbonate box... 1 min before being exposed to an alarm

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in a clear, polycarbonate box (46 cm × 20 cm × 20 cm) covered with a perforated, clear, polycarbonate lid

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the polycarbonate test box during the 5-min alarm exposure.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the polycarbonate test box during the 5-min alarm exposure.

time_to_assay.evidence: All mice were placed back in their cages and were tested 5 min after injection with DPT.

sample_size.evidence: The vehicle group includes new (N = 14) and historical (N = 53) data... cotreatment with NE-100 50 mg/kg and DPT 10 mg/kg (N = 8); other group Ns given only in figures

outcomes.summary: Vehicle-treated Fmr1 KO mice showed 72% AGS prevalence; DPT 10 mg/kg completely prevented AGS whereas 3 and 5.6 mg/kg had no effect. 35% of DPT 10 mg/kg mice showed prolonged wild running and jumping without progression to TCS. Pretreatment with pimavanserin, WAY-100635, SB-224289, methiothepin or NE-100 did not significantly reverse DPT's anti-AGS effect.
outcomes.statistics: DPT 10 mg/kg vs vehicle p < 0.0001 (Fisher's exact); DPT 3 mg/kg p = 0.69; 5.6 mg/kg p = 0.69; WRJ duration vehicle 22 ± 6.26 s vs DPT 10 78 ± 20.7 s, p < 0.01; latency/duration/lethality at 3 and 5.6 mg/kg p ≥ 0.46; pimavanserin 3 + DPT p = 0.10; pimavanserin 10 + DPT p > 0.99; WAY 0.1 + DPT p = 0.33; WAY 1 + DPT p > 0.99; SB-224289 + DPT p = 0.10; methiothepin + DPT p > 0.99; NE-100 30/50 + DPT p > 0.99
outcomes.evidence: vehicle-treated male and female Fmr1 KO mice showed a prevalence of AGS of 72%, and DPT completely prevented AGS at 10 mg/kg (p < 0.0001)... Relative to vehicle, DPT did not significantly affect the prevalence of AGS at 3 (p = 0.69) or 5.6 mg/kg (p = 0.69).

B1_num_measures.evidence: AGS prevalence, WRJ prevalence and duration, latency to seizure onset, seizure duration, lethality: 'DPT did not impact latency to seizure onset, seizure duration, or lethality caused by AGS'

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only session-level prevalence, latency and duration reported; no within-session binned analysis.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: Seizure stages are described qualitatively but no transition/sequence analysis is performed.

B4_ethological.evidence: Seizure was defined by TCS; 'normal behavior' recorded only as a category, not distinct ethological acts.

B5_social.evidence: Assay targets seizure susceptibility, not social behaviour.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate seizure response to a loud alarm; no learning required.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The frequencies of AGS were documented by visual observations of video recordings.

B8_multivariate.evidence: AGS and other behaviors were analyzed using Fisher's exact test.

E2_shelter.evidence: Clear polycarbonate box; no shelter described.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding described in the test box.

E6_spatial.evidence: single clear polycarbonate box (46 cm × 20 cm × 20 cm)

E7_social_context.evidence: A maximum of 4 mice (2 per box) were observed simultaneously; normal behavior defined to include 'socializing'.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described in the test box.

D1_continuity.evidence: the duration of exposure was 5 min

D2_session_duration.evidence: the duration of exposure was 5 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Each mouse tested once, 5 min after DPT injection.

assays.assay_name: Head-Twitch Response and Drug-Induced Behavioural Signs Observation
assays.assay_description: Juvenile (P23-25) and adult (>P60) WT mice injected i.p. with vehicle, DPT (3-20 mg/kg) or DOI (1 mg/kg) and immediately placed in a 43x43 cm open-field chamber; HTRs counted by hand-held tally for 15 min; 5-HT1A-dependent signs (flat body posture, hind limb abduction, tremors, Straub tail) and DPT-induced convulsions (20 mg/kg) observed during the same session.

application_type.evidence: Juvenile (P23-P25) and adult (>P60) mice were injected (i.p.) with Milli-Q water (vehicle) or DPT

setup_habituation.evidence: WT mice were acclimated to a procedure room for ≥30 min before administering test compounds (room acclimation only).

setup_restrain.evidence: were immediately placed in a clear open-field plexiglass chamber (43 × 43 cm; Med Associates)

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the open-field chamber.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the open-field chamber.

time_to_assay.evidence: were immediately placed in a clear open-field plexiglass chamber... HTRs were counted using a hand-held tally counter for 15 min postinjection

sample_size.evidence: juvenile F(5, 23) = 4.25; adult F(5, 22) = 5.18 (implies 29 + 28 animals across 6 groups each, excluding DOI groups); DPT 20 mg/kg N = 10 total WT mice tested

outcomes.summary: DPT produced a biphasic dose-dependent HTR peaking at 10 mg/kg in juvenile and adult WT mice (juveniles: significant at 3-15 mg/kg; adults: 5.6-20 mg/kg); DOI 1 mg/kg produced robust HTRs. Only DPT 20 mg/kg elicited 5-HT1A-dependent signs (flat body posture, hind limb abduction, tremors, Straub tail) and brief tonic convulsions in 90% of mice.
outcomes.statistics: Juvenile: F(5,23)=4.25, p=0.007; DPT 3 p=0.047, 5.6 p=0.007, 10 p=0.007, 15 p=0.046, 20 p=0.287. Adult: F(5,22)=5.18, p=0.027; DPT 3 p=0.391, 5.6 p=0.013, 10 p=0.004, 15 p=0.016, 20 p=0.013 (Holm-Sidak). DOI vs vehicle juvenile p=0.001, adult p<0.001 (t test). DPT 20 vs vehicle: flat body posture 0 vs 90% p=0.0001; hind limb abduction 0 vs 90% p=0.0001; tremors 0 vs 70% p=0.003; Straub tail 0 vs 90% p=0.0001 (Fisher's exact).
outcomes.evidence: In vivo, DPT produced a dose-dependent head-twitch response (HTR), with maximal effects at 10 mg/kg... juvenile and adult mice treated with DPT at 20 mg/kg, but not lower doses, showed distinct behavioral symptoms

B1_num_measures.evidence: HTR count; flat body posture, hind limb abduction, tremors, Straub tail incidence; DPT-induced convulsion incidence

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: HTRs were counted... for 15 min postinjection (session total only).

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No sequence/transition analysis; convulsion progression only described qualitatively.

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR and drug-induced 5-HT1A syndrome signs are not natural ethological repertoire per rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Assay targets drug-induced signs, not social behaviour.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: 5-HT2AR-dependent HTRs were counted using a hand-held tally counter

B8_multivariate.evidence: one-way ANOVA with Holm-Sidak's multiple comparisons test; Fisher's exact tests

E1_environment_type.evidence: clear open-field plexiglass chamber (43 × 43 cm; Med Associates)

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice individually placed in the open-field chamber after injection.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described in chamber.

D1_continuity.evidence: HTRs were counted... for 15 min postinjection

D2_session_duration.evidence: HTRs were counted using a hand-held tally counter for 15 min postinjection

D4_baseline.evidence: Mice injected then immediately placed in chamber; no pre-drug recording.

judge_notes: Retained three assays: AGS test, HTR/drug-induced signs observation, and open-field locomotion (HTR and locomotion kept separate per 2/3 candidates since they assess different behavioural domains).

Merged deepseek4's separate '5-HT1A Behavioral Syndrome Observation' and DPT-seizure observation into the HTR assay: same session, same open field, same observer-scored drug-induced signs (Table 2 footnote states DPT seizure descriptions came from the HTR dose-effect study).
Dropped the NE-100-alone seizure dose-finding observation: NE-100 is not a psychedelic; NE-100 + DPT co-treatment data are covered within the AGS assay.
AGS E7 overridden from 'Alone' (all candidates) to 'Free social group': paper states '2 per box' and lists 'socializing' among normal behaviours during testing.
AGS B1 set to 4-6 (score 2): gemma's score 3 with value '2-3' was internally inconsistent. Locomotion B1 corrected to score 0 (single measure, distance).
HTR D2 = 15 min → score 1 per rubric boundaries (gemma's 0 was incorrect).

setup_habituation set to not_reported for all assays: only room acclimation is described; deepseek's 'yes' for AGS and qwen's 'yes' for HTR relied on room acclimation, and the paper does not explicitly state no habituation.

Dosing list expanded to include the non-psychedelic antagonists (pimavanserin, WAY-100635, SB-224289, methiothepin, NE-100) as the rubric requests every drug compound administered in behavioural experiments.
Age set to mixed (juvenile P23-25 for AGS/HTR; adult >P60 for HTR).
